summary.text: A 67-year-old man with prior myocardial infarction and right bundle branch block presented with 2 days of light-headedness and a syncopal episode with a prodrome of facial flushing, headache, nausea and chest tightness. Physical examination had no notable findings or erythema migrans.

Three troponin I results were below 0.02 ng/mL, BNP was 703 pg/mL and leucocytes were 14 000/mm^(3), resolving the following day. Echocardiogram showed ejection fraction 60–65% without significant abnormality. He subsequently developed persistent complete heart block, with a SILC score of 2 (low risk) at evaluation.

A dual-chamber pacemaker was implanted while Lyme titres were pending, and he was discharged. Titres then returned positive for acute Lyme on western blot and ELISA; on further discussion he reported earlier constitutional symptoms, raising the SILC score to 4, and received 21 days of oral doxycycline.

At 2 months follow-up he had 1:1 conduction and a V-paced burden below 0.1%. With the pacer set to VVI 30, a 14-day event monitor showed no heart block episodes or pacing, and heart rate rose above 150 b.p.m. with 1:1 conduction during exercise. The pacemaker was explanted 23 weeks after implantation; the EKG that day showed normal sinus rhythm with RBBB, and he has done well on more than 1 year of follow-up.
